request:
The indented use is for a private home automation system and private AI harness (open WebUI). As this is for private use we'll use voices (weights) provided by the community - or do not have any license restrictions.

The hardware will be glados.ehrendingen (192.168.0.231); verify if ssh key authentification works. Else set it up together with me.

The architecture of the backend system should support different tts engines - as we currently use VibeVoice in R&D mode - but can not keep this. As we do not know if Fish will meet our expectations the best way forward is to have an architecture that allows to select unti we finished our evaluation.

Can you create a a spec for a prototype and implement and deploy it to glados (English and German); none breaking API contract?
expectations: No breaking endpoint, request, response, header, authentication, or resource-limit changes
No VibeVoice worker or model assets deployed in the prototype
No unreviewed Fish model, voice, or package installed or enabled
No SSH key or host-key changes without exact user-approved scope
No deployment until host identity, SSH authorization, OS/runtime, and network boundary are verified
context: living spec: backend-synthesis requirement scenarios reviewed; record-living-specs helper is unavailable, so the capability spec was read directly
living spec: project-licensing model and third-party material boundaries reviewed
area: backend API request validation, engine dispatch, readiness, tests, and deployment documentation
constraint: preserve existing OpenAI-compatible speech request/response contract
constraint: do not record private target addresses or credentials in feature documents
constraint: SSH host-key verification failed; no remote authentication or deployment performed
constraint: no Fish weights, voices, or runtime installation until exact terms and provenance are reviewed

decisions.decision: Use a fixed engine registry behind SpeechService
decisions.why: The project needs only two in-tree engines; a registry supports selection without an open-ended plugin loader

decisions.decision: Run Fish through a separately managed loopback MessagePack API service
decisions.why: The pinned upstream server uses MessagePack and loads one checkpoint per service; keeping it separate avoids coupling the API process to model startup and memory
decisions.rejected: Embedding Fish model runtime in the backend process or invoking a new CLI process per request

decisions.decision: Add a protected read-only engine catalog and wire the existing vanilla JavaScript UI
decisions.why: The user requested discoverable engine/language/voice choices, and the repository UI is not Vue
decisions.rejected: Expose private paths or modify an external Open WebUI checkout

decisions.decision: Compare Fish variants and defer selection/install until exact terms and evidence are reviewed
decisions.why: Model-size and multilingual claims are not local quality or rights evidence
decisions.rejected: Select a variant solely from parameter count or community availability

decisions.decision: Deploy in parallel on a separately approved port
decisions.why: A healthy service already occupies the current default listener and the user selected side-by-side deployment
decisions.rejected: Replace or reconfigure the existing service

decisions.decision: Deploy macOS baseline in parallel with Fish disabled
decisions.why: The approved prototype preserves the API and runs English/German while exact Fish artifact rights and local evaluation remain unresolved
decisions.rejected: Enable a community Fish checkpoint based only on private-use assumptions or upstream claims

decisions.decision: Leave Open WebUI client settings unchanged
decisions.why: Open WebUI runs on a separate device and its configuration is not in this workspace
decisions.rejected: Modify an external client configuration without its approved path and exact setting scope
